definitions.explanation: A regular tendency or practice that is hard to give up.

examples.japanese: ⟦{毎朝|まいあさ}→毎朝：00966_maiasa⟧⟦{運動|うんどう}→運動：00821_undou⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧{習慣|しゅうかん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: I have a habit of exercising every morning.

⟦{毎日|まいにち}→毎日：00729_mainichi⟧⟦{少|すこ}しずつ→少し：00596_sukoshi⟧⟦{勉強|べんきょう}する→勉強する：00527_benkyousuru⟧{習慣|しゅうかん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦つけたら→付ける：00761_tsukeru⟧、⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{上手|じょうず}→上手：00707_jouzu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: After I developed a habit of studying a little every day, my Japanese improved.

notes:
{習慣|しゅうかん} means habit (personal) or custom (cultural). It refers to regular patterns of behavior.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ～する{習慣|しゅうかん}がある: to have a habit of ~
- {習慣|しゅうかん}になる: to become a habit
- {習慣|しゅうかん}を{身|み}につける: to develop a habit
- {習慣|しゅうかん}を{変|か}える: to change habits

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {生活|せいかつ}{習慣|しゅうかん}: lifestyle habits
- {食|しょく}{習慣|しゅうかん}: eating habits
- {悪|わる}い{習慣|しゅうかん}: bad habits
- {習慣|しゅうかん}{病|びょう}: lifestyle disease

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {癖|くせ}: habit (often negative connotation)
- {慣習|かんしゅう}: custom, convention (more formal)
- {風習|ふうしゅう}: custom, practice (cultural)
